_about: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the fak BENCHMARK SWEEP grid (visuals/61-hero-benchmark-sweep.svg), rendered by tools/hero_sweep_gen.py. fak's analog of the GLM-5.2 'LLM Performance Evaluation' 2x4 bar-grid: one small grouped-bar panel per benchmark, value labels on top, a badge on each bar, the benchmark name in a pill below, the subject (fak) bar in the bright accent. Honesty rules: every fak figure traces to fak/BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md by commit and is the bright bar; each panel compares fak against ONE named, honest reference (a tuned-SOTA baseline, a deterministic ceiling, the optimal, the spawned-hook, or — for capability panels — a field that does not ship it), never a fabricated competitor number. The final panel is the SINGLE-STREAM fence and INVERTS the accent: llama.cpp owns the bright/tall bar, fak shows its honest lower number. Panels lead with Inkling-2-Mini decode and prefill from the public receipts (docs/launch/inkling2-launch-2026-11-24.md, docs/benchmarks/published/), then model-independent kernel axes. Edit this file, then run `python tools/hero_sweep_gen.py`.

desc: An eight-panel benchmark sweep. Inkling-2-Mini on an RTX 5080: decode 118.1 vs 81.0 tok/s for stock llama.cpp in the same window, 119.9 vs 119.5 for the fastest llama.cpp fork (parity), opt-in speculative decode at depth 2 171.5 vs 119.7 plain, and NVFP4 W4A4 prefill 5861 vs 3012 tok/s for the fork on a 512-token prompt (1.95x, prompt rate only). On an M3 Pro, 32-token capitals prompt: decode 40.3 vs 37.5 for Splash and 23.4 for the fastest llama.cpp fork. Kernel: cache invalidation on an external write is bit-exact (max|delta|=0); an in-process guard decision costs 2.4 us against 6.9 ms for a spawned hook, 2,849x. Fence: at 1,946 tokens of context fak decodes 89.0 vs 113.8 tok/s for the fork.
